request.user_prompt: Analyse this SAIL paper and describe the research topics it is salient to.

publication.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Workflow Layer for Research-Team Scientific Assistance
publication.abstract: The paper proposes a Vontology-authored workflow layer for research-team assistants. It argues that persistent knowledge, prompt authority, and workflow telemetry should govern task execution while Python supplies support surfaces. The evaluation studies paper ingestion, topic representation, and user-facing completion reports across repeated research-support tasks.

evidence_spans.text: The paper proposes a Vontology-authored workflow layer for research-team assistants.
It argues that persistent knowledge, prompt authority, and workflow telemetry should govern task execution while Python supplies support surfaces.
The evaluation studies paper ingestion, topic representation, and user-facing completion reports across repeated research-support tasks.
The workflow engine loads represented process graphs from Vontology, validates context mappings, and records turn execution telemetry for replay.
The same representation substrate could later support paper recommendation, meeting preparation, and project memory, but those are downstream uses rather than the central contribution.

topics.rationale: The paper's main contribution is a represented workflow layer for agentic research assistance, so workflow control is central rather than incidental.
The paper explicitly makes persistent represented knowledge and Vontology-authored artefacts part of the execution authority.
Evaluation and telemetry are substantial validation mechanisms, but they support the workflow-control contribution rather than replacing it.
The application domain is research-team support, but the technical contribution is broader than that one use setting.

unsupported_candidates.reason: Mentioned only as a downstream use case in discussion, not as a central paper contribution.
